name: plan_linear_contact
summary: Generate an observation-grounded, TCP-compensated and IK-checked linear contact plan from an explicit surface outward normal.

generality.rationale: Consumes generic point, normal and uncertainty rather than an object class; applicable to buttons, switches, lids and pressable mechanisms.
assumptions: The contact point and surface normal are measured in the world frame.
A short straight-line normal contact is appropriate.
The effector profile provides a TCP rigidly mounted to the arm.
limitations: No continuous collision checking or force feedback.
Does not infer the contact point or surface normal.
Not suitable for sliding, insertion, deformable or torque-dominant contact.

level.rationale: Combines observation provenance, frame-aware TCP compensation, contact geometry and chained IK across four stages.

composition.strategy: Convert a measured point-normal contact into a TCP path, compensate flange-to-TCP geometry and retain only a chained IK-feasible plan.

provenance.failure_gap: Qwen guessed a pixel, depth and servo target because no generic contact planner exposed a provenance-carrying path.
evidence: iter_002 had four servo calls, zero formal plans and native_success=false
iter_007 generated one formal plan from obs_000048 and finished with native_success=true
